title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is Example 3 in a sequence of examples (Ex. 2 precedes it) about what Grothendieck calls 'catégories de Deuring' C over a base ring A. In context these appear to be A-linear categories that are locally (for a suitable topology) equivalent to the category of locally free modules over A, i.e. module categories over Azumaya algebras. In modern language they are categories of twisted vector bundles for a G_m-gerbe.

Ex. 3 adds to such a C an element tau of V_A(C), which seems to be an invertible A-module attached to C through a norm or determinant functor nu: C -> P(A). Grothendieck explains the meaning as follows.
- C generalizes Azumaya algebras over A.
- When A is a domain with fraction field k, an Azumaya algebra over k extends over A exactly when its class lies in Im(Br A -> Br k).
- The pair (C, tau) generalizes the datum of a gerbe with band mu_n.

The left margin gives the dictionary in both directions:
- From a G_m-gerbe on A one gets C = the category of representations of the gerbe of degree n and weight 1 (twisted locally free sheaves of rank n).
- From C one gets back the gerbe of 'admissible' fibre functors from C to locally free modules (a localization of C).
- In the mu_n case, C = representations of degree n and rank 1 of the gerbe, and tau trivializes the determinant (norm). In effect this lifts the G_m-gerbe through the Kummer sequence 1 -> mu_n -> G_m -> G_m -> 1.

Grothendieck then computes the auto-equivalences of (C, tau). Pick an object X of C and put sigma = End(X), an Azumaya algebra of degree n.
- Auto-equivalences are given by sigma-bimodules P that are locally invertible over A on both sides, acting by phi(X) = P ⊗_sigma X.
- They must come with an isomorphism N_{sigma/A}(P) ≅ A, where N is the reduced norm of P, an invertible A-module.
- The margin checks compatibility: nu(phi(X)) = N(P) ⊗ nu(X).
- Locally all such P are isomorphic to sigma (Skolem–Noether).
- These P form a Picard category (a Gr-category, i.e. a 2-group).
- The automorphisms of the unit object 1 = sigma are the scalars lambda in A^* with lambda^n = 1. A scalar lambda acts on N(sigma) = A by its reduced norm lambda^n.
- This Picard category contains Tors(S, mu_n) as a full subcategory, via L ↦ L ⊗ sigma with N = L^{⊗n}.

The aim is a Tannakian-type, gerbe-theoretic description of 'twisted' rank-n categories with determinant data. This belongs to Grothendieck's 1965 programme of a Galois theory of motives with non-neutral fibre functors, gerbes and bands.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The computation Aut(1) = mu_n(A) is consistent: a scalar lambda in the centre of a degree-n Azumaya algebra has reduced norm lambda^n.
The definition of V_A(C) and the exact role of tau rely on Ex. 2, which is not on this page, so the precise construction is partly conjectural.
The neighbouring-page transcriptions are from an unrelated analysis text (deformation of paths, Bourbaki/Dieudonné style), apparently misfiled. They give no context.

ideas.what: Categories locally equivalent to Vect(A) ('Deuring categories') correspond to Azumaya algebras / G_m-gerbes; C = degree-n weight-1 representations of the gerbe, recovered via the gerbe of fibre functors
ideas.modern_name: Twisted sheaves / module categories of Azumaya algebras; Tannakian recovery of a gerbe from its weight-1 representations
ideas.usually_credited_to: Giraud (Cohomologie non abélienne, 1971); twisted sheaves: Căldăraru, de Jong, Lieblich (c. 2000-2008)
ideas.where_published: Brauer group ideas in 'Le groupe de Brauer I-III' (Dix exposés, 1968); gerbe formalism attributed to Grothendieck and developed by Giraud

ideas.what: Pair (C, tau) with a norm/determinant trivialization generalizes a mu_n-gerbe (Kummer lift of a G_m-gerbe)
ideas.modern_name: mu_n-gerbes as G_m-gerbes with trivialized n-th power; SL_n-type structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Giraud 1971; standard in later literature (e.g. Lieblich)
ideas.where_published: Kummer theory for Br appears in Grothendieck's Brauer III

ideas.what: Auto-equivalences of (C, tau) as invertible sigma-bimodules P with trivialized reduced norm N(P) ≅ A; a Picard category with pi_1 = mu_n(A) containing Tors(S, mu_n)
ideas.modern_name: 2-group (Picard stack) of auto-equivalences of a mu_n-gerbe / twisted module category; reduced norm of invertible bimodules
ideas.usually_credited_to: Giraud (band and auto-equivalences of gerbes); Fröhlich and Bass for Picard groups of Azumaya algebras and reduced norms

missed.claim: Archival evidence that already in 1965, in the motivic Galois theory notes, Grothendieck explicitly set up the dictionary between G_m-gerbes and categories of degree-n weight-1 representations (twisted bundles), and between (C, determinant trivialization) and mu_n-gerbes. He also described the auto-equivalence 2-group via reduced norms of bimodules. These are historically early formulations of twisted-sheaf ideas, but they are mathematically standard today.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is history-of-ideas value only. It shows the twisted-sheaf / Tannakian-gerbe viewpoint predates Giraud's book and later twisted-sheaf work, inside the motivic Galois context.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a sketch of standard gerbe/Azumaya/Kummer correspondences, all well covered by Giraud and later literature. The only interest is historical: an early explicit formulation in the motivic Galois notes.
